findings.description: The call-site comment `// A layer adds denials after decision 74's and can never drop one (decision 77).` restates the `ProfileLayer.deny` JSDoc ("they follow decision 74's denials and can never remove one (decision 77)"); per docs/conventions/general.md §Comments (seam-duplication test), delete the call-site copy.

The `deny` check rejects `""` but accepts whitespace-only entries such as `deny: [" "]`, which land in permissions.deny as a rule that denies nothing — the silent failure the parser's comment says it guards against; `tool.trim()` would close it.

The parser comment says a "non-string" rule is not a denial Claude Code can apply, but the check also refuses empty strings; the comment is narrower than the code and repeats the WHY already in docs/03-profiles.md and decision 77.

The test comment `// Decision 77: a layer adds denials after decision 74's and never removes one.` is a third copy of the same sentence; the `describe('layer denials')` block and its test names already say it, so drop it or fold "(decision 77)" into the describe name.

The union idiom `[...new Set([...(a ?? []), ...(b ?? [])])]` now appears four times across mergeLayers and compileProfile (skills, subagents, mcp, and now deny); the new line matches existing style, but the idiom is past the third-use extraction threshold.
